title: An open immersion is fully faithful on the derived categories
statement:
For an open immersion $g:V\hookrightarrow T$, the derived functors satisfy

$$
Lg^*Rg_*\cong\operatorname{id},
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
Lg^*i_*=0
$$

for the closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ of $g$.

proof.text: The inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]. Use the already proved source-library rightDerivedFunctorCompMapDerivedCategoryIso with F = g_* and G = g^* to identify Rg_* followed by D(g^*) with R(g_* followed by g^*). This generic comparison uses the canonical Grothendieck-category K-injective-resolution instance; no separately stated resolution or preservation theorem is required here.

The open-immersion sheaf counit is an isomorphism by [lem-sc-open-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful]. Apply the source-library rightDerivedFunctorNatIso to this counit, then rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory for the identity and mapDerivedCategoryIdIso. Composing these natural isomorphisms with step 1 proves D(g^*) Rg_* is naturally the identity. The exact-functor identification is [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization].

The complement equation implies Disjoint (range g) (range i). The functor i_* is exact because a closed immersion is finite, and g^* is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]. Thus i_* followed by g^* is exact. For every integer n, [lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowerstar] kills its value on H^n(K). The source-library isZero_mapDerivedCategory_obj, using commutation with homology and detection of zero objects by homology, therefore makes D(i_* followed by g^*)(K) zero. Transport along mapDerivedCategoryCompIso, supplied by exact-functor descent [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], to obtain the asserted second composite.
